question.prompt:
A rectangular piece of paper \(6\) inches wide is folded as in the diagram so that one corner touches the opposite side. The length in inches of the crease \(L\) in terms of angle \(\theta\) is:

[Figure 1](figures/1972_AMC_12_Q30_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
A fold acts as a reflection across the crease. In particular, the crease bisects the segment joining the original corner to its folded position and is perpendicular to that segment. These facts let us use the paper's width in a right triangle.

[Figure 1](figures/1972_AMC_12_Q30_question_fig1.svg)

Name the original bottom-right corner \(A\), the top-right crease endpoint \(B\), the bottom crease endpoint \(C\), and the point where the folded corner touches the left side \(D\). Thus \(BC=L\). Let \(E\) be the bottom-left corner, so \(AE=6\).

The fold sends \(A\) to \(D\) and fixes \(B\) and \(C\). Therefore the crease \(BC\) bisects the angle between \(BA\) and \(BD\). The marked angle is \(\angle DBC=\theta\), so \(\angle CBA=\theta\) as well.

Write \(AC=a\), and let \(N\) be the intersection of \(AD\) with the crease. Reflection gives \(AN\perp BC\) and \(AD=2AN\). Since the bottom and right edges of the rectangle are perpendicular, \(\angle ACN=90^\circ-\theta\). In right triangle \(ACN\),
\[
AN=a\sin(90^\circ-\theta)=a\cos\theta,
\]
so \(AD=2a\cos\theta\).

Also, \(AD\perp BC\) and \(AE\perp AB\), so \(\angle DAE=\theta\). Right triangle \(AED\) now uses the known width:
\[
6=AE=AD\cos\theta=2a\cos^2\theta.
\]
It follows that \(a=3/\cos^2\theta\).

Finally, triangle \(ABC\) is right at \(A\), with hypotenuse \(BC=L\) and angle \(\theta\) at \(B\). Thus \(a=L\sin\theta\), and
\[
\boxed{L=\frac{3}{\sin\theta\cos^2\theta}
=3\sec^2\theta\csc\theta}.
\]
The shown nondegenerate fold has an acute \(\theta\), so the sine and cosine denominators are nonzero. The answer is choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
solutions.title: Track the reflected corner with right triangles
